description:
Proposal (approved 2026-11-07): /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-exceptions.html, published at https://claude.ai/artifact/EsjTtpXU3kJqaChtmgP7Sv. Research fact sheets (Elixir 1.20.5 surface, OTP 30 emulator, OTP 30 compiler) are summarised on the page.

Goal: an fz program can catch what it raises, with Elixir's semantics, on interp, run and build. Signal: Elixir-oracle fixtures for every try form, and the existing abort fixtures gaining rescuing twins once fz-sc8.64 names the library's exceptions.

Design in one paragraph: the process gains a handler stack. fz_panic keeps its signature; its contract becomes "deliver (kind, value) to the nearest handler if one is active, else render the line and fail" (the empty-stack case is #278 unchanged). try lowers in body.rs in the vocabulary receive uses: a body block, a handler closure template (outer continuation + captures) pushed on entry and popped by the body's continuation, a dispatch over (kind, __struct__) for the arms, one join. after and else are desugarings (nested try + re-raise, as v3_core does); no runtime concept. Rescue dispatch is over __struct__ only (five legal Elixir shapes); normalisation is identity because every fz failure is a struct after fz-sc8.63/.64; ErlangError wraps a panic of a non-struct. Kinds error/throw/exit share the stack with one tag. defexception waits on fz-sc8.77 (__struct__ at runtime).

Decisions taken with approval: __STACKTRACE__ evaluates to [] inside rescue/catch and is a compile error elsewhere (documented difference). throw/exit/catch are the third ticket. Own epic, based off 243d62f89 (#278 head); rebase onto fz-sc8.63/.64 when they land. panic/1 stays public.

Working rules: one worktree /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-exceptions; one PR stacked on #278, one commit per ticket pushed as each closes; every ticket updates .agent/docs and fixtures docs for what it adds; gate per ticket is RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 cargo test --workspace --all-targets, doc tests, clippy -D warnings, fmt --check; no pin or golden rises without a measured explanation brought to the coordinator; deferrals need prior authorisation.

comments.text: Sequencing: based off 243d62f89 (#278 head) now by the user's instruction; rebase onto fz-sc8.63/.64 when they land. The abort fixtures' rescuing twins come with that rebase (needs .64's exception names).

2026-11-09, coordinator fz-xxd13-build-8d: stack #274's prefix #268-#284 (develop through fz-sc8.62) is SQUASH-MERGED into develop (develop now 4bab6bba1, tree identical to 678f06df1). PR #280 was retargeted to develop but still carries the pre-squash commits, so GitHub shows it CONFLICTING and CI will not run. The fix is a pure rebase with no conflicts (trial-run: resulting tree identical to 13688c71a): in /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-exceptions, git fetch origin && git rebase --onto origin/develop 678f06df1 fz-3ul/exceptions && git push --force-with-lease=fz-3ul/exceptions:13688c71a origin fz-3ul/exceptions. Separately, before #280 lands: its fixtures 00733-00739 and 00750-00793 (51 files) sit in fz-sc8's block, and 44 of those numbers are taken on develop's upcoming stack (#285 and up) by other fixtures; git reports no conflict because the names differ. Renumber them into fz-3ul's block 00800-00899. The fz-sc8 stack above develop is now #285 (.57) through #294 (.10, head a3bc3efce).

title: Exceptions: try, rescue, catch and after over the one failure route
